description: The settings.set no-op case (S44 T5): a value that is ALREADY the stored value writes nothing and reports changed=false — a re-set of the same value must not stamp a new audit row, so a client that watches the history sees no phantom write. The SettingView is still returned (the row the value resolves to), so the UI can confirm "this is already set"; changed=false is the signal a caller uses to skip a re-write. set is the only door that changes a value, and a no-op is not a change (P31's one-resolution rule: the answer is the store's own, never a handler-rewritten one).
